task.title: Reconcile the board renderer instead of replacing every card each poll
task.description:
Replace the boards destroy-and-rebuild render with a keyed reconciliation that only touches what changed. This is the structural fix behind WB-01KZC3BGYFHYKE2GZPD191H555; that ticket carries the diagnosis and a one-line CSS mitigation, this one removes the cause.

## Why this is worth doing properly

render() rebuilds every column from scratch on every one-second poll: a fresh DocumentFragment of new card nodes and list.replaceChildren(fragment) (internal/webui/assets/index.html:1806-1808), driven by setInterval(refresh, 1000) at :1957. Every card node on the board is destroyed and recreated once a second, almost always producing identical DOM.

Measured against the projects own board in Chrome 151, 69 cards present. Holding a reference to a card across a single poll: heldStillConnected false, sameNode false. Nothing survives.

Three user-visible defects fall out of that single behavior, all confirmed by measurement, not inference:

1. Columns self-scroll. A column scrolled to 2994 walked to 3916 over ten polls, about 76 to 93 px per tick, and eventually parks itself at the bottom. Cause is browser scroll anchoring reacting to the churn: .task-list is a scroll container (index.html:46) and nothing sets overflow-anchor, so the default auto applies. Proven by isolation: replaceChildren with byte-identical clones, no data change whatsoever, drifted 472 px over six iterations, while editing text in place on the same nodes produced one legitimate 36 px adjustment and then held steady.

2. Keyboard focus is destroyed every second. Cards are focusable (article.tabIndex = 0, index.html:338). Focused a card, waited one poll, and document.activeElement was BODY. The board cannot be keyboard-navigated at all: focus is lost faster than a person can act on it. This is the most serious of the three and is an accessibility defect, not a polish issue.

3. Drag state is lost mid-drag. dragstart adds is-dragging to the node (index.html:1900) and there is no render guard for an active drag, so a drag lasting longer than one second has its source node detached and replaced. Measured: is-dragging true before, the live replacement node has it false, original node detached. The card visibly stops looking dragged while still being dragged.

There is also a standing cost with no upside: 69 cards rebuilt 60 times a minute for as long as a tab is open. The is-refreshing opacity flash (index.html:47, 1809) exists only to paper over this churn and can likely go away with it.

## Work

1. Reconcile by task ID. Cards already carry data-task-id (index.html:338), so the reconciliation key exists. In render(), diff the desired per-column task list against the nodes present and apply the minimum: create nodes for new IDs, remove nodes for departed IDs, reorder survivors with insertBefore, and update survivors in place. Preserve node identity for any task whose rendered content is unchanged.
2. Update card content in place. Factor card() (index.html:337) into a builder and an applier so a surviving node can be updated without being recreated. Fields that change: title, description, priority, labels, ID prefix, dependency summary, aria-label. Bail out early when the tasks projected value and its presentation view are both unchanged from what the node was last rendered from; stashing the last-rendered values on the node or in a WeakMap makes that check cheap.
3. Keep the two render entry points working. render() is called from rerender() (:1474), which the optimistic queue drives at :1491, :1516, and :1521, and from refresh() (:1844). Both must go through the same reconciliation. Note projectTasks returns the input array unchanged when no intents are pending (:1464-1465), which is a free fast path.
4. Guard or correctly handle a render during an active drag. Either skip reconciliation for the dragged card while activeDrag is set, or preserve is-dragging across an update. Do not let the dragged node be detached.
5. Preserve focus. If a focused card must be recreated, restore focus to its replacement. If reconciliation is correct this should rarely trigger, but the guarantee should not depend on that.
6. Keep overflow-anchor none on .task-list as a defensive guard once WB-01KZC3BGYFHYKE2GZPD191H555 adds it, so a future code path that rebuilds a column cannot silently reintroduce the drift.
7. Reassess is-refreshing. With reconciliation the flash has no reason to fire on an unchanged poll. Remove it or scope it to columns that actually changed.

## Testing

The existing client tests run in a fake DOM with no layout engine, so they cannot observe scroll drift. They can, however, observe the property that actually matters, because node identity is a DOM-level fact and needs no layout. Assert directly:

- A task whose data did not change keeps the same node across a render. This is the contract whose violation causes all three defects and it is fully testable in the current harness.
- A changed task updates in place and is still the same node.
- An added task appears, a removed task disappears, and neither disturbs its neighbours identities.
- A reordered column moves existing nodes rather than recreating them.
- A focused card retains focus across a render.
- A render during an active drag leaves the dragged node connected and still marked is-dragging.

A real-browser check for the scroll behaviour itself is optional given the above, but if one is added, drive Chrome over CDP: scroll a column, sample scrollTop across ten polls, assert it is unchanged.

## Dependency

Depends on WB-01KZBT3J1AMW4E5F688WPNZGJZ. That ticket changes queue semantics (detail-form expectedHead, stale-write re-base) and its fixes land in the same drainIntents and rerender path this work restructures. Doing the correctness fix first means the render path is restructured once, against settled semantics, rather than twice. It is also the right order by severity: the queue bug silently loses a collaborators edits, while these defects are visible and lose no data.

The CSS mitigation in WB-01KZC3BGYFHYKE2GZPD191H555 is deliberately not blocked by any of this and should ship immediately.
